text:
nora: Heads-up — onboarding `big-rlhf-v2` ONNX to staging failed readiness checks. Serving runtime rejects the model at load time, claiming a kernel/ops mismatch and tokenizer/weights inconsistencies. Putting logs below.

samir: can you paste the exact error? quick guess: either the ONNX export changed op set or tokenizer vocab didn't match the LM head.

nora: Error dump from the container:```
[2026-03-15 14:04:12] runtime ERROR: Triton backend init failed: no suitable kernel for operator 'multihead_attention' for compute capability 8.6
[2026-03-15 14:04:12] modelloader ERROR: missing initializer: lm_head.weight (expected shape [50257, 4096], found 50260)
Traceback (most recent recent frames trimmed)
```

maria: that first line smells like a Triton/CUDA mismatch (kernel recipe compiled for a different sm). which container tag was used?

nora: using `redwood-inference/runtime:2026-03-10-gpu-cuda12` (the default canary). ONNX file is at s3://redwood-models/big-rlhf-v2/onnx/model.onnx and tokenizer at s3://redwood-models/big-rlhf-v2/tokenizer/fast_tokenizer.json

samir: two parallel things to validate: (1) weights/LM-head alignment with tokenizer vocab_size, (2) runtime kernel compatibility with opset/compute capability.

zach: for (1) check the onnx graph initializers list: run `python -c "import onnx; m=onnx.load('model.onnx'); print([i.name for i in m.graph.initializer if 'lm_head' in i.name])"` and verify shapes with `numpy` if needed. also confirm tokenizer `vocab_size` and `bos_token_id` are set.

nora: did that, output shows `lm_head.weight` present but shape `50260 x 4096`. tokenizer reports `vocab_size: 50257` (from the fast tokenizer). so mismatched export.

samir: That explains the missing initializer error path — runtime expected 50257 entries but ONNX has 50260. Likely multiple special tokens added at export, or merging of added tokens wasn't synced. Two fixes: re-export the model with explicit `vocab_size`/`add_tokens` handling, or re-save tokenizer to match the weights. Which is easier now?

nora: re-export is quick on my side. question: when we re-export, should we use `use_fast=False`? the fast tokenizer remove/merge quirks have bitten us before.

maria: we prefer the `use_fast=True` for perf in-host, but for model parity, explicitly setting `add_prefix_space` and saving `vocab_size` in the tokenizer config is safer. if you run `tokenizer.save_pretrained(..., legacy_format=True)` you can preserve python tokenizer's fields. alternatively, set `--force-vocab-size` in export script.

zach: I'll take the container/kernel angle. The Triton kernels we compile require CUDA toolkit and target SMs in the build matrix. The canary runtime image was built with CUDA 12.1 toolchain and Triton 2.21 baked-in. The staging nodes are Ampere with SM 8.6 but our prebuilt kernels were compiled without the newer fused-mha op enabled for that SM. Two options: (A) rebuild runtime container with the extra kernel flags (longer), (B) fall back to non-Triton CPU/runtime kernel (slower) for now. Which do we want for the canary?

nora: fallback would be fine for a short window, but we need a final answer for production onboarding. Also re-exporting to match tokenizer is independent — can be done immediately.

samir: action plan: Nora re-exports ONNX with matching tokenizer settings and pushes artifacts to `s3://redwood-models/big-rlhf-v2/onnx/` with a `-v2` suffix. Zach will try a quick runtime rebuild on a test image with `--enable-fused-mha` and `-arch=sm_86` or alternatively adjust Triton build matrix. Maria will validate tokenizer save flags. I'll coordinate canary deployment once both sides confirm.

nora: re-export command I'm running:```bash
python scripts/export_onnx.py \\
  --model-checkpoint s3://redwood-models/big-rlhf-v2/checkpoint.pt \\
  --out s3://redwood-models/big-rlhf-v2/onnx/model-v2.onnx \\
  --force-vocab-size 50260 \\
  --tokenizer-save-args '{"use_fast": false, "legacy_format": true}'
```
will ping when uploaded.

ci-bot: build started for `runtime-rebuild-sm86-2026-03-15` (job 4321) — logs: https://ci.internal/build/4321

zach: quick notes for the rebuild (to self / CI): Dockerfile snippet to tweak:```Dockerfile
ARG CUDA_TOOLKIT=12.1
ARG TRITON_VERSION=2.21
RUN build_triton --version $TRITON_VERSION --cuda $CUDA_TOOLKIT --extra-cflags "-arch=sm_86" --enable-fused-mha
```
I'll try the above in a disposable image and test model load.

samir: if rebuild hits issues, fallback plan: patch runtime to accept mismatched vocab by mapping out-of-vocab entries to `unk_token` at load time as a temporary compatibility shim (low perf but unblocking). probably a 1-day patch.

maria: re tokenizer: Nora, please also include `tokenizer_config.json` with `bos_token`, `eos_token`, and `vocab_size` explicitly. that avoids fast tokenizer autoguess.

nora: done — uploaded `model-v2.onnx` and `tokenizer-v2/` to s3. hash: sha256:abc123... starting a quick load test against canary fallback route.

ci-bot: model pkg `big-rlhf-v2:model-v2` uploaded and indexed (pkg id 9876).

zach: test load log after rebuild trial (local test):```
2026-03-15 16:10:01 runtime INFO: loaded model big-rlhf-v2 model-v2 on triton backend
2026-03-15 16:10:01 runtime INFO: kernel selection: fused-mha (sm_86)
2026-03-15 16:10:02 runtime INFO: tokenizer vocab_size 50260 matches lm_head 50260
```
looks good locally. I'll roll the rebuilt image to a single staging node for integration tests.

samir: thanks everyone. follow-ups:
- nora: confirm E2E generation test passes by EOD (owner: nora)
- zach: push runtime canary container and update canary pool (owner: zach)
- maria: verify tokenizer files in artifact registry match runtime assumptions (owner: maria)
- samir: I will schedule a 15-min sync tomorrow to close the roll.

nora: E2E quick smoke passed (greedy + sampling checks). no logits anomalies in short seqs. :tada:

zach: canary updated to `runtime:2026-03-15-sm86` on 1 node, monitoring for 30m then expand. metrics look normal.

maria: checked tokenizer packaging, `tokenizer_config.json` present, `bos_token_id` set, fast tokenizer hash matches offline export.

samir: great — leaving this thread open for a bit, but looks like we resolved the mismatch and kernel issue. closing action items tomorrow unless someone objects. :thumbsup:
